routes.description: Establish a defensible prior framework, support the principal historical data through reliable testimony, and show that their conjunction is more expected if Jesus rose than under the relevant competing explanations.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the historical sources warrant the central burial, empty-tomb, appearance, and witness data, the resurrection hypothesis has a non-prohibitive prior, and its comparative likelihood for the combined data exceeds the alternatives.

motionBridge.description: Connect the supported historical data and prior considerations to the conclusion that resurrection is more probable than the competing hypotheses.

centralBridges.description: Establish that the relevant texts and testimonial traditions provide sufficiently reliable access to the claimed historical events.
Establish the death and burial, empty tomb, reported appearances, conversions, and costly witness conduct as data requiring comparative explanation.
Show that mistake, hallucination, fabrication, continued burial, and comparable rival accounts predict the combined data less well than resurrection.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Supply background reasons concerning divine agency and incarnation that prevent the resurrection prior from being evidentially insurmountable.
Support the durability and sincerity of the reported experiences while distinguishing those properties from the final historical inference.

routes.description: Apply demanding but claim-sensitive historical standards, challenge the reliability and independence of the proposed data, and deny that comparative or Bayesian framing can supply warrant absent adequate support for the event itself.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the claimed death, tomb, appearances, or transmission remain insufficiently established, or if the inference from those reports to resurrection fails to exceed natural alternatives and rational uncertainty remains available.

motionBridge.description: Connect deficiencies in the data and inference to the conclusion that the historical evidence does not make resurrection more probable than competing hypotheses.

centralBridges.description: Require source proximity, independence, corroboration, confirmed witnesses, and evidence proportionate to the extraordinary character of the claim.
Challenge whether death, burial, an empty tomb, appearances, and accurate transmission are independently established historical data.
Distinguish reports, sincerity, transformation, and expected evidence under resurrection from evidence that resurrection actually occurred.
Preserve an unknown or unconvinced conclusion when exhaustive hypotheses lack sufficiently grounded probability assignments.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Separate whether the event occurred from claims about God, supernatural mechanisms, present miracles, or other alleged returns from death.
Test whether selective disclosure, obscure testimony, and sacrificial means fit the divine background assumptions used to support the prior.

sections.title: Probability Method, Priors, and Rational Uncertainty
sections.rationale: This issue governs how the historical material may update an initial probability, whether qualitative likelihoods are usable, and whether the largest member of an exhaustive set warrants belief or leaves uncertainty.

sections.title: Source Reliability, Independence, and Transmission
sections.rationale: The resurrection comparison depends on whether the New Testament writings and underlying testimony provide sufficiently early, independent, corroborated, and accurately transmitted access to the alleged events.

sections.title: Death, Burial, and Empty-Tomb Foundations
sections.rationale: Death, placement in a known tomb, and subsequent emptiness form a central evidential sequence, while disputes over confirmation determine whether that sequence is available for explanation at all.

sections.title: Appearances, Memory, Sincerity, and Transformation
sections.rationale: Reported encounters and witness conduct supply a principal affirmative datum, but their force depends on memory, identification, sincerity, transmission, and the distinction between committed belief and truth.

sections.title: Competing Explanations and Supernatural Context
sections.rationale: The motion requires comparing resurrection with mistake, hallucination, fabrication, and other explanations while determining whether divine agency, incarnation, modern miracles, or analogous claims legitimately affect that comparison.
